data.narrative:
Lunar Energy, a Series D climate and energy company founded by Kunal Girotra, has raised over $300M to date. The valuation assessment draws from a comparable universe of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private peers (Redwood Materials, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy) alongside one public comparable, with additional reference to a broader peer set including Helion and QuantumScape.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $300M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 1.5x Series D step-up multiplier, implies a $450M valuation. Peer-median analysis, based on four comparables with valuations ranging from $700M to $6.0B and a median of $2.0B, implies $2.0B. The wide peer range ($700M–$6.0B) reflects material heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital efficiency within the climate tech sector.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $382M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median point of $1.2B. The 6x spread between low and high estimates reflects uncertainty inherent in early-stage climate technology valuations, including unresolved commercialization timelines and the sensitivity of comparable valuations to private market sentiment. Stage-progression anchors to actual capital deployment, while peer-median captures market pricing for similar-stage players; the tension between these methods represents the key valuation uncertainty.
